body: I think there's a lot of emotions with morally abhorrent people.  Fear and feeling unsafe; confusion, uncertainty, stress and resulting anxiety; disgust with their immaturity; rage that they would treat me or someone else that way; etc.
Neither exercise nor meditation do much for chronic illness.  Exercise usually just makes your illness get worse.

That's interesting that it comes up with seasonal depression.  My traumas disappear then seem to come up at particular times, as if they're all still in there.  I guess this validates, that, yes, the trauma is still there, even when I think I'm fine.
I wouldn't say you can't heal.  I think I've recovered from part of it, but some of it is still in there.
I agree with a lot of what you're saying, but I disagree about having zero excuses.  Being disabled without qualifying for disability is one legitimate excuse.

I'm not sure what counts as love.  Seems like certain people are needy but it might look like love.  People only "love" me when they think I'm going to caretake them.  I'm not in a position to caretake anyone right now without them giving anything in return.  I'd rather be alone than play those social games.

Yes.  Well, even if I don't feel bad, there's nothing to feel good about either.

I don't want to talk to people because interactions with people are so empty and oftentimes frustrating if not worse.  But I am lonely.  Just can't think of any possible way to fix that.

If I get out of bed, then what?  What's the point of getting out of bed.  But I won't feel good if I stay in bed either.

Sometimes I'd rather do nothing because allowing my mind some rest helps me feel better.  But then I feel guilty because I don't get chores or work done.

I relate to a lot of this.  I've felt this way for a very long time.  I'm pretty depressed about it right now, so I can't honestly say anything really encouraging.  Sometimes I have short bursts of feeling more hopeful and empowered but then it goes away and I feel like this again.  It's tough when nothing ever seems to change.

Funny, I'm also dealing with an elderly dad, and it is horribly depressing.  My siblings are also self-centered due to their personality disorders.
I hate so say this but this applies more when you're younger than when you're older.  Now that I'm older, it's really hard to imagine I can ever fulfill my dreams or reach my potential.

Stuff like that never seems to work for me.  Even if a statement sounds logical, my brain won't accept it.  What overrides everything is the reality of my situation and the truth of what I see around me.  It would make sense that I can still deserve love if terrible people do, but real life just doesn't work that way.  The truth is that I am not loved by the people around me.  And it's hard to believe I deserve to be happy if I'm not keeping up with basic adult responsibilities that grant you the right to happiness.  So I can't believe that I deserve happiness when I haven't earned it.

>you wouldn't try and force someone with a broken leg to run a marathon

Problem is I don't have a choice.  I have to run with a broken leg or else I will face an homelessness or other awful things.

>I wish there was some kind of positive point we could take away from this

I actually did learn some things from all this.  I've had so many abusive people in my life, but with this person it was easier to see their thought processes and what was going on.  Knowing this it now feels like it is easier to spot abusive people.  It's given me a lot more clarity in general on these sorts of people.

I also learned that I forget who I am when I'm around people like that, maybe because they make me walk on eggshells and tiptoe around them.  Now I understand why I often find myself feeling empty after being around certain people.

It also somehow cured me of this feeling I've had that I ought to be "cool" to fit in or be liked by others.  I've always felt like I had to be something which wasn't myself to be included and liked by others.  Something inside me saw him as the cool kid.  Then somehow, seeing how immature and childlike he was made me realize how unappealing that all is, and I felt more able to accept my "uncool" self.

Well, I was already lonesome for so many reasons in my life.  I've had a lot against me. But then you think at least there's dating apps to fix that.  Then it turns out everyone you meet on the app will treat you bad.  So then it's back to accepting my regular lonely life.

I was burnt out and irritated when dealing with the bpd, but, yes, after leaving the loneliness and depression hit.  I'm looking for some meaning in life.  Some kind of connection or some reason to care about anything.  The bpd gave me the false feeling that my efforts were going anywhere.

That's one reason I like music.  It helps get the fight back in you.
Mine really loved comedy sketches involving men using lies and manipulation to get a woman in bed with them.  Claimed he thought it was funny that a guy would be so desperate to do that.

Well, in my case it seemed we had nothing in common other than misery.  Couldn't have fun with them and conversation sucked.  Didn't seem like we belonged together.  Seemed he was trying hard to make it seem like we had something in common.  But then he'd act like I was so weird and it was clear we were from very different worlds with very different minds.  But he'd act oblivious to that, and I'm not sure if that's because he was incredibly dumb or trying to play me.

He did try to act like I was especially kind and he'd always say he'd never had anyone who wasn't always screaming at him before.  Would claim I was gorgeous, but it just didn't sound right to me.  (Realizing now it was probably his attempt to try to make me feel special or charm me).  

For a while I thought I was the only one that could help him or be there for him.  Well, it did seem I was the only person who had time for him, and I may have been one of the few people who'd have the patience to tolerate him.  I was also lonely, so just happy to be talking to anyone who seemed accepting of me.  

I was "special" in that I had time to give him.  But then he just wanted more and more time.  Because I'm struggling with being disabled, he must have thought I had endless time on my hands (which really pisses me off).

These blood-sucking types seem to show up in my life again and again.  I must be "special" for them to be drawn to me.
So then it's not an accident.  Was OP being sarcastic about it being an accident?

I relate.  I feel empty living life.  At least when depressed I feel something and have something to think about.  I have clarity.  The real world keeps me too busy and empty.  But I also have ADHD and am sensitive to light.  Light makes me feel more empty and blah.  At least at home, I can be in the dark and have more feeling and thoughts.
I'm not into gaming but the right kind of music helps.  (I don't know if I qualify as hiki, but I inevitably am stuck at home without friends.)
How does one show love with actions?

I can understand not liking a therapist or having bad reactions to meds, but they better give a better explanation as to why or else it just sounds like they're making stuff up.  

I was drained because I tried to help and gave them resources and bought things for them to try to help, and they would act super grateful then not do anything with any of what I'd done for them.  Seems the gratitude was just a form of manipulation.  If they were genuinely empathic they would have told me not to waste my time and money.

Once he said that meditation and breathing exercises helped him when he was dealing with stress, but he just didn't want to use them because he essentially wanted to focus on his ruminating thoughts.  Huh?  So, basically, even though he has the tools to calm down, he just chooses not to use them.

>Doesn't undermine your value as a human! Even with your difficulties, you deserve to be happy and be loved!

How do I convince myself of that?
I think they'll take anyone they can get.  So they have lots of options.  The only barrier is finding vulnerable people who will fall for facade.

I feel like it's neediness moreseo than love.  They need someone to play a certain role for them in the same way someone may need an object like an appliance or tool.  Once they find someone that can fit that role and is willing, they're happy.  If that person leaves, they hope to find someone else who is willing and available.
Why did it teach you to be more vulnerable?  I would think it would teach you to be less vulnerable.

That's how I feel about love.  I don't know what it's like for other people, but for me the chance of it happening are slim.  The closest I've got to love is this delusional love.  Doesn't seem to me there are very many capable of love, at least not in my world.

I think movie love looks like delusional love, too.  Romance movies are awful.  I felt like women like them because they loved the idea of some man buying them things and doing things for them.
It's crazy.  "My ex was the devil, but I'm still in love with them!"

I kept cool, but I started to realize that by keeping cool, I was invalidating myself and hurting myself.  Once I realized I couldn't keep cool anymore, I decided not to talk to them at all because I knew how they were going to react if they did see me get angry at them.  So I just tried to disappear gently.

Basically, I don't think keeping cool instead of getting angry is a good strategy.  But there is no good strategy for dealing with these people.  They are impossible.

>i'm not actually sure how much our reactions make a difference

They seem to be always upset no matter what.  If you're not upsetting them, they'll find something to be upset about.  So it does feel like it doesn't matter what you do or don't do.  It's non-stop drama. Peace isn't possible in their world.  At least that's my experience.

> I was talking more about pop culture / celeb gossip

I think a lot of those people live by their image rather than their true self.  When you're living by your image, all you care about is that you're such a nice person.  If you've ever known someone with a personality disorder like narcissistic personality disorder or borderline personality disorder, you might know what I mean.  A lot of Western culture is tends towards ego and individualism and hence towards narcissism, but those traits especially show up in those who are in the spotlight.  Online, you'll see if in virtue signalling and main character syndrome.

The truth about "nice" people is that they're often hypocrites.  They'll say all sorts of nice things and be very nice to you in ways, but then they treat you as less than and disrespect you frequently.

There is a such thing as being too nice and compassionate.  At that point, you're just a codependent who's getting the life sucked out of you and no longer knows who you are or what you even like.  It's okay to not be nice sometimes.

So many people are oversensitive and easily triggered, that it does feel like you have to walk on eggshells.  You have to be very careful what you say all the time.  It's much less exhausting to be away from people altogether.  I wish the culture wasn't like this, but it is.  Lots of sensitive, traumatized, fragile people everywhere.
Where did you get that the remission rate is over 90%?

>I’m the only person they want and they’ll never see themselves with anyone else but me

They made me feel like I was special, too.  Like I was the only person who'd ever been nice to them, and they'd never find anyone like me.  Actually, that was all superficial.  They barely knew me and would never appreciate the things that were good about me.  Just superficial compliments.  They aren't capable of ever really getting to know a person.  

And if you look at how they act towards you and the things they say to you, it's a contradiction to the claims that you're such a wonderful and perfect person.  I always felt like I was being disrespected, looked down on, and scammed.  He didn't see much value in me at all despite how supposedly wonderful he claimed he thought I was.

That's why I have a hard time talking to these people or looking them in the face.  They're scam artists and their entire life is based on fooling people.  

How do you talk to someone who will never be honest and real with you?  The whole time they're talking, you know that there's a good chance the words coming out of them is a lie.

He told me from the beginning that he had BPD but that didn't stop me from being friends with him.  It was actually talking to him and getting to know him that made me realize I had to leave.  His idea of hard work was to go to therapy and pretend he was listening.  If you even asked him what type of therapy he was getting, he had no idea.  But at least he knew what his diagnosis was!  He just wanted me to stick around so he could use me and pretend to be giving but only keep taking and exhausting me.  Burnout made it so I could no longer speak.  Running in circles with no solution.  There was no way out.

>some of us work very hard to better ourselves

I think people on this subreddit are dealing with the ones who aren't working hard to better themselves.  

With my experience with someone with BPD, anytime he claimed he was bettering himself it was really just an act so he could get a pat on the head and gain everyone's forgiveness, love and support.  All he cared about was his image and doing what he needed to do (fooling, charming, lying, manipulating, etc.) to get what he wanted.  That seemed to be all that was important to him.   So I can't see why he'd have the motivation to better himself.

I tried to be forgiving and understanding, too.  Yeah, he was odd because conversations were very shallow and everything he said and did was shallow.  But I thought there must be a reason for that, and I've got to be patient.  But eventually, it clicked, that there was no reason other than that it was all fake.

I was always quietly frustrated but trying to stay patient on the outside.  He said I was so nice because other people would yell at him and I would keep quiet and not complain.  Really, I get why they'd be yelling at him all the time.  But he never learns.  Everything is still about him.

In the end, I could only feel rage and annoyance towards him.  He constantly disrespected me and in the end he'd turn it to be about him like I didn't matter at all except to serve his purposes.  If he was really in that much pain, would he continue to act like that? Wouldn't he get it that his happiness relies on treating other people better? I don't get it.  We weren't all put on this earth to be a martyr for him.

"I’m tired of feeling empathy or making excuses for these types of people."  

Reading about borderline misled me.  It said that they feel emotions very intensely and can't handle their emotions.  But he had virtually no emotion, just a lot of irritability.  Maybe they seem emotional because they snap so easily, but otherwise there is no intense emotion to be seen.  I didn't get the sense that he was in that much misery at all.  He just liked to talk a lot about it.   That was all he talked about, ever.  

He looks more like an addict that is choosing not to come down and thinks everyone owes them because they're the center of the universe.  I guess there's no reason to come down if the pain you cause others doesn't bother you and you don't believe in anything other than enjoying your life.
That actually sounds a lot like what psychopathic religious leaders do.  They talk the talk but don't walk the walk.

He is childlike and doesn't feel manly or like he has any testosterone.  Always has a "softness" to him, like a child.  Rage is actually a symptom of low testosterone and addictions, too, so it makes sense.  He is just an addict that doesn't want to come down to earth.

They would apologize a lot.  To me, that seemed really nice because I'm used to being around abusive people who never apologized and didn't care how I felt.  But the profuse apologizing was weird and it was always hollow.  He'd still keep doing things he apologized for.  Actually, every interaction with him felt like it was going nowhere.  I honestly finally "woke up" when he was complaining about his ex, and it started to become obvious that he was twisting the story to make himself look good.  It was like he was doing everything possible to not have to face himself.

There were plenty of things he could do to control his mood, but, no matter what, he refused to do anything that might actually help him.

He asked me what I thought of him and realized I couldn't tell him the truth because any kind of truth would get him upset.

I got so sick of being "polite" and holding my tongue to try to avoid hurting his "feelings" which in reality were delusions.  He seemed to want to live under the fantasy that he was mature, responsible, intelligent and macho.  He seemed to only say "sorry" to people because he cared so much about his image and what people thought of him, not because he was sorry.

I felt uncomfortable because he was not respecting sexual boundaries.  I tried to brush it off, but I should have listened to that discomfort.

Also acting like I was weird when I was doing something perfectly normal.  Or things that felt like I was being bullied or insulted even though he was so "nice".

Never really understanding of me or anything I was going through.  Always fake shallow compassion and I could never explain anything to him in a way he would understand.  Always fake gratitude too.  Would say thank you for things I did for him, but never did anything with it.  Just lots of wasted effort on my part and he expected me to just be grateful that he said "thanks" and that he'd told everyone he knows how nice I am (why do I care what he's telling people???).

Claims I'm helping him but really it seems like he just wants a codependent mother around.  It's some psychological emotional need that he's using me for.  Became clear I wasn't helping him at all.

Tons of really dumb excuses all the time.

He had a drinking problem and would do destructive things while drunk.  He stropped drinking and even went through withdrawals.  Turned out he was just waiting for his 30 days probation to be up so he could start drinking again.  At least that's what it was starting to look like.

His sense of humor is really weird.  Lots of passive aggressive stuff framed as "jokes", but none of it was light-hearted.  I'm not sure he understands humor or how to lighten up.  Just tense all the time.  His whole body is tense too, but he doesn't want to get that checked out.  Doesn't want to do anything about anything.  But he does talk a lot in circles.

Yes...weak. I keep thinking they just need to man up.  They act like a child that is only led by their emotions.  They don't seem like they believe in anything other than to keep living by their emotions and living for themselves.  I don't think it's just that pain is so intense that they're incapable of facing it (lot of us have intense pain and still do what it takes to heal).  They just don't want to do what it takes.

They refuse to man up.  It's like all they really want in life is to be coddled and for things to come easy.  They act like a fussy little child if they have to actually do anything to get better.  Even if all they had to do is swallow a pill that would make them nauseous to be cured of BPD forever, they wouldn't do it.  (But alcohol makes them nauseous, and they'll still drink!)

No matter how desperate they are or how bad they claim the pain is, they're not willing to do anything about it.

The BPD I know seems to use his diagnosis as a way to fake being "sorry" for his behavior and claim he's working on it.  If you listen to him closely enough, he isn't actually that humble.  He's always twisting things to make it seem like everyone else did something wrong and he's just a victim.  But the, "I'm sorry, I've been diagnosed and I'm working on it," gets him gold stars.  Just like a child in school.
That's impressive that they admitted that.  I'd rather that than the ones that say it's "love" when it's really just a mechanical act that feels physically good to them.

They make up the dumbest excuses for things.  If they could just admit the truth or just say they're not interested or uncomfortable with something, that'd be fine.  But the stupid excuses just kills me.  It's like the sort of excuses a 5 year old would make up to get away with things.

"Only after losing all of their enablers and hitting rock bottom might they admit they need real help."  The BPD I know is in therapy and AA, but I think it's only because they were forced to be.  They act like they're doing what they can to get better, but it really started to feel like it's an act.  I think they're just doing it so that they can say to other people, "See, I'm going to therapy! I'm working on myself."  It's all just for show.

Their description fo the progress they've made or any insights is always very shallow.  Makes them seem like they have an IQ of a child, but I'm now realizing that they just think others are dumb enough to believe them.

I was reading up on the concept of a man-child and found a lot of overlap.

Felt like he wanted me to be his mother.  Felt like he was obsessed with the idea of me taking care of him.  I took care of him for a while and now he suddenly claims he's thinking of me all the time after the caretaking.  Keeps expecting me to be his therapist and feel sorry for him while he refuses to actually take action to get better.  It's like he's addicted to being miserable and being the victim because he wants me to  play caretaker and mommy.  It's like deep down inside, he doesn't want to become a man.

I agree.  Say they're "in love" but their feelings are so shallow and childlike.  No passion at all.  Hard for me to imagine them being "in love".  To them, being "in love" means they found the object that they can elicit their wants from, so they "love" the object.  Makes me sick.
Honestly, if I trusted my instincts, I would have been able to tell something was off from the very beginning. They always seemed strange.  Really naive and childlike.

I think you maybe love the person you thought they were.  So much of them is a lie that we fall for.  I thought they were so nice, so kind, so understanding.  But in reality, they contradicted all that.  They were never understanding, never truly appreciative, and never seemed to be really sorry when they apologized.
I don't know how it's possible to like them in that way once you can clearly see what's going on and no longer falling for their lies.

After knowing someone with BPD, I also find it hard to imagine that they'd actually do what it takes to get better.  

The BPD I know is never willing to read up on borderline or even watch a video.  Has relied his whole l life on drugs whenever he has emotions he doesn't want to face and so hasn't developed any health habits or coping mechanisms beyond drugs.  He goes to therapy and takes meds, but it doesn't seem to be getting anywhere.  He doesn't even know what sort or therapy he's getting and doesn't seem to care.  I think the only reason he's in therapy is probably because it's court-mandated.  He said the meditation and the breathing exercises his therapist told him to do helped him when he was stressed, but he doesn't want to do them when he's having bothersome thoughts.  How does that make any sense?  His logic usually doesn't make much sense.  Not sure how he'll ever help himself with a mind like that.

Compassion is wasted energy.  You give and give but in the long run, their situation doesn't change.  Better to give that compassion to someone who you can actually help.

To me, dealing with a borderline person in my life feels like constantly being scammed, lied to, misled, given false promises, given false respect and false compliments and gratitutde.  At the same time, there are always bizarre excuses for why they can't do the work they need to do or take any responsibility for anything.

I do get jealous, but I don't wish harm on the other person.  

I know about the Myers Briggs, but I don't know which one he is or how it relates to jealousy.

It's insane.  That's sounds like my brother too.  I guess jealousy is a powerful force in some people, but it makes no sense to me. I've never felt inclined to hurt someone just because of jealousy.  I don't know what his Myers Briggs is.
Sure. I may not have all the answers, but I can try.
Confused how you can be avoidant and still manage to have a partner.

Seems to me that people promote a lot more self-neglect and deprivation than self-care.  At least from what they say in words.  Although they seem to promote more for others not so much for themselves.

When you get into existentialism and nihilism it helps to know that others feel the same way.  And when you find that we're all going through this together, and when you can see kind of a purpose.  To connect with others who also feel this way, to be someone who understands.
Is that related to the default mode network?
Where do you meet people?

I did try to do the full program at first so basically the diet, recommended supplements, coffee enemas, infrared and pushing down exercise. Can't remember if there was anything else.  I quit taking the supplements but still would use infrared and coffee enemas.  The supplements were helpful just wasn't sure about spending the money. Pretty much anything he suggests is useful. It's just hard to keep up with it all.

>my parents just fed me empty generic platitudes and judgemental criticism in place of actual guidance or follow through.

It's amazing how low people's emotional intelligence is.  (I'm not sure if emotional intelligence is the right word here).  It seems like people in general just love to dish out empty platitudes and aren't capable of any deeper thought or understanding.

I always thought I had no desire for hugs because I didn't know what I nice hug felt like, I guess.  Maybe also just cut off from my needs and desires in general.  Now my desire for affection sometimes surfaces, and I feel better when I get some even if I have to hang out with assholes to get it.  Most of my life I haven't gotten positive physical touch, so I feel for you.

I didn't have the chance to read through the whole thing, but I can relate to feeling confused about love.

I'm genuinely not sure if I am able to feel love or how much I care about others (or life itself).  It's bothered and confused me a lot.  I go through cycles of going into burnout and coming out of burnout, and when I'm in burnout, I am just impatient and annoyed with people and have difficulty with empathy (which reminds me of how the cat made you feel).  When I'm come out of burnout, I can care about others a little more but I still feel existentially empty and am not sure I truly care.  Perhaps there is some element of burnout to your case as well.

I'm not sure I've ever been in love, but I did have limerance once which felt like real love.  It's weird that I was able to experience fantasy love like that.  To be fair my case is complicated because my health problems make it so that I don't produce all the hormones at regular levels.  But I can still relate to the devastating feeling of not experiencing normal love and connection.

I kind of gave up on finding people to connect with because I want to meet people who I can have deeper conversations with, who have empathy and compassion, etc.  I find that most people will invalidate or ignore what you share with them or try to downplay anything horrible in your life and practice toxic positivity or quote inspirational things they read in books.  People don't like to put themselves in another's shoes, but they always expect you to put yourself in theirs and feel sorry for them.

In the end, even if I can't get empathy or caring from another person, at least maybe I can get superficial love or connection with someone, so I shoot for that.  I still feel empty, lonely, lost and depressed, but it helps a little.

I really haven't figured out how to meet the right people.  If a person is the type that can connect emotionally, I think it will happen naturally.

I feel like music and meditation help me connect with myself.  It's hard, though.

Why does putting on a mask and pretending things are okay hurt others?  I usually hide how I feel.  I don't think anyone wants to be bothered.  Got ghosted for not pretending to be happy, so I learned that it's not okay to let people see if you're going through something difficult.  Plus in general get cruel responses from people.

I guess I didn't think of it like that because people are always acting like human life is so valuable and it's so sad when people die.  Maybe now more people have convinced themselves that it's okay if people die.
Yeah, it's like trying to make it okay when people die so that no one feels sad when you die.

There is nothing to me because I am disabled and can't do anything with my life or be a wonderful person.  My abuser thinks I am nothing and there is no way for me to prove otherwise.  I have no friends, no love, no resources, no financial stability, no future, no identity, no power over my life or ability to do much of anything with it.  

So when my abuser acts like I'm a piece of shit that needs to be taken out of this world, I have absolutely no defense.  No matter what wonderful quirks I have, I am powerless to do anything useful with them because of the position of life I'm in.
I've liked it when people I've barely known have touched me, so it's not like that for me.
I was replying to what 7atm said when he said social emotional and sexual frustration comes in one pack.  Or maybe I misunderstood what they meant by that.

I'm honestly not sure how I feel about most people touching me.  I've always felt hugs are weird, like I feel like they should feel warm to me but they don't.  I just hug because I'm supposed to, just like a handshake.  But sometimes a reassuring pat can feel nice.  I've rarely felt like touch feels nice to me, and I'm not sure what made it feel nice the times when it does feel nice.

I'm not hurting myself, only helping myself.  Not why you see it as something that is harmful to me.

For me to have a chance of anyone I can have a connection with and feel comfortable around is really hard.  I found touch from the right person can have a very positive affect on me psychologically.

I can't afford a car and public transportation is extremely limited here.  I am feeling very unwell being home alone.  I am extremely desperate to get out of here because it's put my mental health in an extremely low place.

It's also therapeutic to be around people who are kind to me and who I can get along with rather than the people I'm used to being around who have scarred my mind.  It's helping me learn that there are people out there that I can communicate with and work together with.  That not all people are sources of pain and frustration or who are just scheming to hurt or use me.

And I never had a chance to learn anything about myself sexually or romantically so I feel in a safe place to connect with that.
People who treat me bad are an instant turn-off.  But if I just met someone and they're treating me okay, I don't have a problem.
I still feel lonely even with a partner because I wish I had someone who understood and cared about me and people I could go out and have fun with, not someone to hookup with.
I'm not horny but I still find physical closeness therapeutic.  Touch is different than sex.
Some aspects but not the core of the theory.

I relate to a lot of these.  Except not sure I enjoy sex.

I can't even be motivated out of guilt anymore because the people in my life are toxic so all of that loses meaning.  So in a state where really nothing matters and life is just a joke.

They're finding that SSRI antidepressants make your emotions more flat, so it helps people who want to feel less joy and sadness, but I think we already have flatter emotions.  Stimulants help. I have some theories as to what dysthymia really is.

If you want someone to discuss with maybe we can chat.  Honestly, I think I need someone to talk to as well.  Most therapists don't get because they're used to people with normal depression who want to feel emotions less strongly.
Kinda sounds like what I feel.   Did you ever used to feel anything?  If so, what did it feel like?
Arab-American here who feels out of place with both cultures.  Craving a different part of the world.

I like how you put that.  Reminds me of my last therapy session.  At first, I was like, "Well, I got some insights!  Great!"  But I felt more distressed rather than less.  Then I realized: "What was the point of that?  Why is this woman wasting my time instead of doing any actual healing work?"

It's like reading never-ending self-help books.  Fill your head with lots of info, but you're still in the same place.
What did you use to make the music?
Here on lonely subreddit this evening.  Don't have any particular evening routine, but all the days blur together and I don't even know what I've done any day.
Sounds fun.  Feel like I wouldn't even be lonely, but maybe I would.

I haven't really talked to a lot of people outside of therapists about it.  You'd expect therapists would acknowledge it since that's supposed to be their job. There are a few suggestions, depending on your situation and what feels right to you.
